# True-facet erosion excludes the symmetric triangle counterexample family

This is an actual endpoint-compatibility obstruction. It uses the true
three facets of the middle triangle, rather than only its aligned outer
support triangle. It does not resolve the corresponding branch for an
arbitrary middle body.

Throughout, area is two-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Put

    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1),
    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for i=1,2,3}, |T|=9/2.

For 0<L<=3 define the actual triangle

    K_L=conv{(2,-1),(-1,(1+L)/2),(-1,(1-L)/2)}.

Its centroid is zero, its area is k=3L/2, and its actual aligned
outer support triangle is -T. In particular

    h_(K_L)(-v_i)=1 for all i,
    h_(K_L)(v_1)=2,
    h_(K_L)(v_2)=h_(K_L)(v_3)=(1+L)/2.             (1)

Here h_D(u)=max_{x in D} u.x denotes the support function.

## 1. Exact true-facet erosion and the volume credit

**Theorem 1.** Let A,B be planar convex bodies, B contained in T,
and (A+B)/2 contained in K_L. Fix any source y in R^2 and suppose
each of the three lines

    v_i.x=2v_i.y-1

meets int A. Then, writing a=|A| and b=|B|,

    b/k < 1-L^2/81.                               (2)

If additionally k<=a+b, then

    a/b > L^2/(81-L^2).                           (3)

Consequently a<b/32 and k<=a+b are incompatible with these
geometric hypotheses whenever L>=9/sqrt(33).

*Proof.* The three true facet normals of K_L, normalized to have
support value 1, are

    u_1=(-1,0),
    u_2=((3+L)/(2L),3/L),
    u_3=((L-3)/(2L),-3/L).

They sum to zero and have rank two. Let b_j=h_B(u_j) and put

    rho=(b_1+b_2+b_3)/3.

There is a unique z satisfying u_j.z=b_j-rho for all j: the
right sides sum to zero, and the sole relation between the u_j
is their displayed sum. Therefore

    B contained in z+rho K_L,
    2K_L minus_M B := {x:x+B contained in 2K_L}
                   =-z+(2-rho)K_L.                (4)

The symbol in (4) is only the explicitly defined Minkowski
erosion. These identities follow by applying each of the three
facet inequalities; there are no omitted directions because K_L
is exactly their intersection. Since B has positive area,
rho>0. Since the erosion contains the body A, 2-rho>0.

Properness gives

    h_A(-v_i)>1-2v_i.y.

Containment in the erosion and (1) imply

    h_A(-v_i)<=v_i.z+(2-rho).

Sum over i. Both sum v_i.y and sum v_i.z vanish, so
3<3(2-rho), that is,

    0<rho<1.                                     (5)

Write D=z+rho K_L. By (1),

    sum_i h_D(v_i)=rho(3+L).

Choose an index i with h_D(v_i)>=rho(1+L/3). The width of D
in the same unnormalized linear coordinate v_i.x is at most
3rho, because all three widths of K_L in (1) are at most 3.

We use the following elementary cap estimate. For any convex
body D, linear functional f of width W>0 and maximum h, and
c<h, the cap {f>=c} has area at least

    ((h-c)/W)^2 |D|,

provided c is no lower than min_D f. Indeed, choose a point of
D where f=h and contract all of D toward that point with ratio
(h-c)/W. The contracted copy remains in D and has f>=c.
Open and closed caps have the same area because a line has
zero area. If c<min_D f, the entire body is captured.

Here B contained in D intersect T has positive area, so the
case 1<min_D v_i.x cannot occur. Removing the cap outside
v_i.x<=1 and using |D|=rho^2 k gives

    b/k <= rho^2 - [(rho(1+L/3)-1)_+]^2/9.        (6)

The right side is strictly increasing for 0<=rho<=1. Below
rho=1/(1+L/3) it is rho^2. Above that value, its derivative is

    2rho(1-(1+L/3)^2/9)+2(1+L/3)/9>0,

since 1+L/3<=2. Apply (5) to (6) to obtain (2). If k<=a+b,
then a/b>=k/b-1, which with (2) gives (3). Finally
L^2/(81-L^2)>=1/32 is equivalent to 33L^2>=81. This proves
the last assertion, including the equality endpoint because
(2) and (3) are strict. QED.

For the exact ordinary counterexample L=15/8, the true normals
are (-1,0),(13/10,8/5),(-3/10,-8/5). The bounds specialize to

    b/k<551/576,
    a/b>25/551>1/32 when k<=a+b.                  (7)

Thus that actual ordinary K-source example cannot be completed
to the small-A compatible configuration. This conclusion does
not use genuine mixed criticality or common cap budgets.

## 2. The cap/profile hypotheses exclude the remaining thin parameters

Let the source be reflection-fixed,

    y=(x,-x/2) in int K_L,
    R=(2-x)/3 in (0,1).

Let q_i be the area of K_L intersect {v_i.w>=v_i.y}. Set

    c=128/279,
    F=q_min+q_mid+q_max/4.

**Lemma 2.** If q_i<=c k for all i and F<=k, then L>8/5.

*Proof.* The first cap is the triangular tip at (2,-1), so
q_1/k=R^2. Since c<(17/25)^2, we have R<17/25.
Reflection (x,y)->(x,-x-y) fixes the body and source and gives
q_2=q_3.

If the horizontal cut lies below both vertices on x=-1, that
is R<1-L/3, its missed triangle has relative area
9R^2/(9-L^2), and hence

    q_2/k=1-9R^2/(9-L^2).

For fixed R and L<3(1-R), this is at least its value at
L=3(1-R), namely 2(1-R)/(2-R). Consequently it is strictly
greater than 16/33 when R<17/25. Since 16/33>128/279, this
case is impossible. The equality-boundary formula is the same.
Thus only the upper vertex lies above the cut, and

    z:=q_2/k=q_3/k=(L+3-3R)^2/[2L(L+3)].         (8)

Suppose for contradiction that 0<L<=8/5. If z>=R^2, the
sorted profile is R^2+(5/4)z. Completing the square, or
minimizing this quadratic in R over the whole real line, gives

    F/k >= 5(L+3)^2/[8L(L+3)+45]
          =1+3L(2-L)/[8L(L+3)+45]>1.

If z<=R^2, the profile is 2z+R^2/4. This expression strictly
decreases with R on 0<R<=17/25 and 0<L<=8/5: writing
D=L(L+3) and A=L+3, its derivative is

    -6(A-3R)/D+R/2<0.

For example A-3R>=3-51/25=24/25, D<=184/25,
and R/2<=17/50 make the sign immediate. For fixed such R,
the derivative of z with respect to L has the sign of

    R(2L+3)-(L+3).

This is at most (9/25)L-24/25<=-48/125<0. Therefore

    F/k >= [2z+R^2/4]_(L=8/5,R=17/25)
          =2(256/575)+289/2500
          =57847/57500>1.

Both cases contradict F<=k. This proves L>8/5. QED.

## 3. Actual incompatibility of the whole symmetric-source family

**Corollary 3.** There are no planar convex bodies A,B and
reflection-fixed source y in int K_L satisfying all of:

* 0<L<=3, B contained in T, and (A+B)/2 contained in K_L;
* every line v_i.x=2v_i.y-1 meets int A;
* q_i<=128k/279 for all three middle caps and F<=k;
* a<b/32 and k<=a+b.

Indeed Lemma 2 gives L>8/5, and (2) yields

    b/k<1-64/2025=1961/2025<32/33.

But a<b/32 and k<=a+b give b/k>32/33. This is a contradiction.

The corollary is limited to the displayed family and to its
reflection-fixed sources. Theorem 1 itself holds for any source.
It neither supplies an arbitrary-body support-filling converse
nor assumes that the ordinary counterexamples are mixed critical.

## 4. The actual pentagon counterexample is excluded as well

The same true-facet argument tolerates a quantified outward change
of the middle body. Suppose an actual body K is contained in
z_0+sK_L. Retain B contained in T, compatibility (A+B)/2 contained
in K, and the three proper A cuts through any source as in
Theorem 1. Define rho and z using the true normals u_j of K_L
and the support values of B. Then

    B contained in z+rho K_L,
    A contained in 2z_0-z+(2s-rho)K_L.

Summing the three strict proper-cut support inequalities gives

    rho<2s-1.                                    (9)

The same cone-cap argument gives

    b/|K_L| <= f_L(rho)<f_L(2s-1),
    f_L(r)=r^2-[(r(1+L/3)-1)_+]^2/9.            (10)

The strict monotonicity proof for f_L works for every r>=0;
in particular there is no restriction 2s-1<=1. The hypotheses
imply 2s-1>rho>0.

Now take L=15/8 and the actual pentagon

    K^+=conv(K_L union {(1999/1000,-1),
                         (1999/1000,-999/1000)})

from the ordinary cap/profile counterexample. In its three true
triangle-facet directions, its support values are

    h_(K^+)(u_1)=1,
    h_(K^+)(u_2)=h_(K^+)(u_3)=10003/10000.

Thus K^+ is contained in z_0+sK_L, with

    s=5001/5000,
    z_0=(1/5000,-1/10000).

The exact area computation in that counterexample also gives
|K^+|=s|K_L|. Since 2s-1=2501/2500, (10) yields

    b/|K^+| < f_(15/8)(2501/2500)/s
            =127640941/133360000
            <32/33,                              (11)

where the last gap is 55368947/4400880000>0. Hence the actual
pentagon, despite its positive-length contacts on all three
aligned support facets, also cannot satisfy a<b/32 and
|K^+|<=a+b together with the actual endpoint compatibility and
proper cuts. No middle cap-criticality is needed for this
specific incompatibility certificate.

## 5. A shape-dependent criterion for an arbitrary triangular middle fiber

**Theorem 4.** Let K be any triangle whose actual aligned outer
support triangle is -T; equivalently h_K(-v_i)=1 for each i.
Let A,B be convex bodies satisfying B contained in T and
(A+B)/2 contained in K. Suppose all three A cuts at
v_i.x=2v_i.y-1 are proper, for any one source y. Put

    S=sum_i h_K(v_i),
    W=max_i [h_K(v_i)+1],
    zeta=((S/3-1)_+)/W.

Then

    b/k < 1-zeta^2.                              (12)

In particular, if zeta^2>=1/33, these hypotheses are incompatible
with a<b/32 and k<=a+b. A simpler sufficient shape condition is

    S>=3+9/sqrt(33).                             (13)

*Proof.* Translate K to its centroid and denote the centered
triangle by K_0. Its three facet normals can be normalized as
u_j.x<=1 with sum_j u_j=0: explicitly, its barycentric coordinates
are (1-u_j.x)/3, whose sum is one. Apply the exact true-facet
construction of Section 1 to B. There are rho>0 and z such that

    B contained in z+rho K_0,
    A contained in 2g-z+(2-rho)K_0,

where g is the centroid of K. Since
sum_i h_(K_0)(-v_i)=sum_i h_K(-v_i)=3, summing the three
proper-cut support inequalities again gives rho<1.

Translation does not change either the sum S or the individual
widths. Thus D=z+rho K_0 has sum_i h_D(v_i)=rho S, and every
one of its three widths is at most rho W. The same cap-contraction
estimate gives

    b/k <= rho^2-[(rho S/3-1)_+]^2/W^2.          (14)

Here S>0: after centering the triangle, all its support values in
nonzero directions are positive. Moreover W>=S/3+1, by averaging
the three widths of K. Therefore the right side of (14) strictly
increases for rho>=0, by the same derivative calculation as in
Section 1. Evaluating it at rho=1 proves the strict (12).

Since K is contained in -T, every h_K(v_i)<=2, and therefore
W<=3. Condition (13) gives zeta>=1/sqrt(33). Finally (12)
and k<=a+b imply a/b>zeta^2/(1-zeta^2)>=1/32, which is the
claimed contradiction. QED.

No assertion here derives (13) from the ordinary cap/profile
conditions for a general triangle. The symmetric-source family
is the case for which Section 2 proves a sufficient condition.

## 6. The small-A regime forces an actual triangle vertex near an outer corner

Use the hypotheses of Theorem 4 and additionally assume

    a<b/32,  k<=a+b.                              (15)

Introduce the barycentric coordinates of the outer triangle -T,

    lambda_i(x)=(v_i.x+1)/3,  sum_i lambda_i=1.

**Theorem 5.** Either K contains a vertex of -T, or a vertex of K
lies on an edge of -T and has one of its two nonzero barycentric
coordinates strictly less than 1/63. The other coordinate is
therefore strictly greater than 62/63.

More precisely, if K has no outer vertex, label its vertices P_i
so lambda_i(P_i)=0, and define

    m=min_{i!=j} lambda_i(P_j)>0.

With the erosion parameters rho and h=2-rho from Theorem 4,

    m < ((h-1)/h)/(1-a/(h^2 k))
      < 32h(h-1)/(32h^2-1)
      < 65/4097 < 1/63.                          (16)

*Proof.* If K has no outer vertex, a vertex of K can lie on at
most one outer edge. Every outer edge contains an actual support
contact of K; that contact face contains a vertex of K. There
are exactly three vertices and three edges, so the three contacts
are three distinct vertices. No edge contact can contain two
vertices of K, because that would leave too few vertices for the
other two edges. Thus the indicated labeling is possible and all
off-diagonal lambda_i(P_j) are positive.

Write the actual enclosure from the true-facet erosion as

    A contained in p+hK,  h=2-rho.

For each i, properness supplies an actual point a_i in A with
v_i.a_i<2v_i.y-1. Pull it back to X_i=(a_i-p)/h in K and set

    epsilon_i=[2v_i.y-v_i.p+h-1]/(3h).

Then lambda_i(X_i)<epsilon_i, so epsilon_i>0. The normal sum
gives the exact total slack

    sum_i epsilon_i=(h-1)/h.                     (17)

Write X_i=sum_j q_(ji) P_j. The matrix Q=(q_(ji)) is
nonnegative and column-stochastic. Since lambda_i(P_i)=0,

    m(1-q_(ii))<=lambda_i(X_i)<epsilon_i.

Let L=I-Q. Its columns sum to zero, so det L=0. Every principal
2-by-2 minor is nonnegative, since

    1-q_(ii)>=q_(ji),  1-q_(jj)>=q_(ij).

The characteristic-polynomial identity in dimension three gives

    det Q=det(I-L)
         =1-tr L+sum(principal 2-by-2 minors of L)
         >=1-tr L
         >1-(sum_i epsilon_i)/m.                 (18)

The triangle conv{X_1,X_2,X_3} is contained in the pulled-back
body (A-p)/h, and its area is |det Q| k. Hence

    a/(h^2 k)>=|det Q|>=det Q
               >1-((h-1)/h)/m.

In particular the argument does not assume a favorable orientation
of the selected triangle. Rearranging yields the first bound in
(16), since a/(h^2 k)<1.

Indeed B contained in a homothet of K of scale rho<1 gives
b<k, so a/k<1/32. Also (15) gives b/k>32/33. Since b/k<=rho^2,

    sqrt(32/33)<rho<1,
    1<h<2-sqrt(32/33)<65/64.

The last rational inequality follows from
(63/64)^2<32/33. The function

    32h(h-1)/(32h^2-1)

is strictly increasing for h>1: its derivative has numerator
32(32h^2-2h+1)>0. At h=65/64 it equals 65/4097. Finally
65*63=4095<4097. This proves (16) and the stated geometric
alternative. QED.

The conclusion is a quantitative contact classification. It does
not identify the other two vertices with points on the opposite
outer edge and does not impose reflection symmetry on the source.
Those further restrictions would exclude possible triangles and
are not used here.

## 7. Exact exclusion when the middle triangle has no outer vertex

Retain the hypotheses of Theorem 5, with y in int K. Suppose also that the three
middle caps through the same source y satisfy

    q_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y}|<=128k/279.

Then K must contain a vertex of -T. This conclusion uses neither
the sorted profile F_K nor an unproved assertion about which
triangle vertices the three caps capture.

### 7.1 The source-dependent placement credit

Let W_i=h_K(v_i)+1 and r_i=(1+v_i.y)/W_i. Since the source is
in int K, r_i>0. Write the true-facet enclosures in the original
coordinates as

    A contained in p+(2-rho)K,
    B contained in -p+rho K.

The three proper A cuts give individually

    v_i.p<1-rho+2v_i.y.

Consequently the outer homothet D=-p+rho K has

    h_D(v_i)>rho W_i-1-2v_i.y,
    width_i(D)=rho W_i.

The elementary cap contraction against B contained in T gives

    b/k <=rho^2-(rho-2r_i)_+^2
          <1-(1-2r_i)_+^2.                       (19)

For clarity, if rho-2r_i>0, the actual support excess is strictly
greater than W_i(rho-2r_i); if that quantity is nonpositive,
the trivial bound b/k<=rho^2 suffices. The last inequality
follows from rho<1: the displayed function of rho has derivative
2rho before the positive part becomes active and 4r_i afterward.

Since (15) gives b/k>32/33, (19) implies

    r_i>(1-1/sqrt(33))/2>41/100.                 (20)

In outer barycentric coordinates, let m_i=max_K lambda_i=W_i/3.
Then (20) states

    lambda_i(y)>(41/100)m_i.                    (21)

The source term has not been discarded: lambda_i(y) is retained
in every inequality, and no assumption y=0 is made.

### 7.2 An exact triangular quantile lower bound

Consider one affine coordinate on a triangle with vertex values
0,l,m, where 0<=l<=m and m>0. Put t=l/m. If its cap at a source
coordinate z has relative area at most c=128/279, direct triangle
area gives

    z/m>=phi_c(t),
    phi_c(t)=1-sqrt(c(1-t))       if t<=1-c,
             sqrt((1-c)t)       if t>=1-c.       (22)

The first case cuts off the unique high vertex; in the second
case the missed triangle is cut off at the low vertex. At the
transition the formulas agree. Thus (22) includes both possible
vertex incidences and their boundary case.

Put b_0=sqrt(1-c)=sqrt(151/279). For every 0<=t<=1,

    phi_c(t)>=(3b_0-1)/4+(1+b_0)t/4.             (23)

In the first branch, write u=1-t. The claim follows from

    (1-b_0)+(1+b_0)u/4>=sqrt((1-b_0^2)u),

which is the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality. In the second
branch, let w=sqrt(t). If A=(3b_0-1)/4 and B=(1+b_0)/4, then
b_0=A+B and

    b_0 w-A-Bw^2=(1-w)(Bw-A)>=0.

Indeed w>=b_0 and B b_0-A=(1-b_0)^2/4>=0.

Since b_0>147/200, (22)--(23) imply the convenient rational
bound

    z>=A_0 m+B_0 l,
    A_0=241/800, B_0=347/800.                   (24)

The rational comparison follows by squaring positive numbers:
(147/200)^2<151/279.

### 7.3 The actual near-corner contact matrix is incompatible

Suppose K contains no outer vertex. By Theorem 5 and relabeling
the coordinates and contact vertices, its three vertices have
outer barycentric coordinates

    P_1=(0,p,1-p),
    P_2=(r,0,1-r),
    P_3=(s,1-s,0),
    0<p,s<1,  62/63<r<1.                       (25)

No condition on which of the two nonzero entries in each row
is larger is imposed. Define

    T_0=41/100,
    G(x,y)=max{T_0 max(x,y),
               A_0 max(x,y)+B_0 min(x,y)}

for x,y>=0. The actual placement bound (21) and the ordinary cap
bound (24) imply

    1=sum_i lambda_i(y)
      >=G(r,s)+G(p,1-s)+G(1-p,1-r).             (26)

The function G is nondecreasing and B_0-Lipschitz in either
coordinate separately. To verify this, the first expression in
its defining maximum has slopes 0,T_0, and the second has slopes
A_0,B_0. All are in [0,B_0]; taking their maximum preserves the
same monotonicity and Lipschitz bound. Therefore

    G(r,s)>=G(1,s)-B_0(1-r),
    G(p,1-s)>=G(1,1-s)-B_0(1-p),
    G(1-p,1-r)>=T_0(1-p).

Also G(1,s)>=A_0+B_0 s and
G(1,1-s)>=A_0+B_0(1-s). Sum these estimates to obtain

    sum G>=2A_0+B_0-B_0(1-r)-(B_0-T_0)(1-p)
          >=2A_0+T_0-B_0(1-r)
          >2A_0+T_0-B_0/63
          =1+283/50400>1.                       (27)

This contradicts (26), proving the exclusion.

The exact outer-vertex case is not obtained by silently assigning
the remaining two vertices to the other two outer edges. At an
outer vertex, two support contacts coincide, and the third vertex
of K may lie elsewhere. That contact stratum is separate and
remains outside this section's conclusion.

## 8. A stronger source bound closes both triangle contact strata

The exact outer-vertex case left in Section 7 can also be excluded
when the cap bound is sharpened using the actual endpoint masses.
The resulting proof is shorter than the contact classification and
does not use it. The matched support hypothesis K_out=-T remains
explicit; it is not automatic for a general canonical three-fiber
configuration.

**Theorem 6.** Let K be a triangle with h_K(-v_i)=1 for all i,
and y in int K. Let A,B be convex bodies with B contained in T,
(A+B)/2 contained in K, and all three A cuts
v_i.x=2v_i.y-1 proper. Suppose a<b/32 and k<=a+b. It is then
impossible that all three middle cap areas satisfy

    q_i<=65k/144.                                (28)

*Proof.* The true-facet erosion gives rho<1 and b/k<1 as
above. The inequalities a<b/32 and k<=a+b give b/k>32/33,
so the source-dependent placement proof in Section 7.1 yields

    lambda_i(y)>(41/100) max_K lambda_i           (29)

for all i. These statements do not distinguish exact and nearly
coincident outer support contacts.

For any one of the three outer barycentric coordinates, its
values on the vertices of K are 0,u,v with 0<=u<=v and v>0.
The zero is present because this is an actual support direction
of K. Its value at the ordinary centroid g_K is (u+v)/3.
If lambda_i(y)<=lambda_i(g_K), then (29) implies

    t:=u/v>23/100.

The cap area is nonincreasing in its threshold. Its fraction at
the centroid threshold is exactly

    (2-t)^2/[9(1-t)]          for 0<=t<=1/2,
    1-(1+t)^2/(9t)           for 1/2<=t<=1.      (30)

This is the same direct triangle-area calculation as (22), now
at the centroid threshold. On the first interval its derivative
is t(2-t)/[9(1-t)^2]>=0. On the second interval its value is
at least 1/2: equivalently 2(1+t)^2<=9t for 1/2<=t<=1.
Thus t>23/100 forces

    q_i/k >=31329/69300>65/144.                 (31)

The last comparison is exact:
31329*144=4511376>4504500=65*69300.
This contradicts (28). Consequently lambda_i(y) must be
strictly greater than lambda_i(g_K) for every i. Their respective
sums are both one, which is impossible. QED.

**Corollary 7 (actual common-cap budget).** In the same matched
support setting, set

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B).

Thus these are exactly the three fibers whose area is counted.
Consider the actual ambient caps whose middle
traces are v_i.x>=v_i.y, whose A traces are
v_i.x>=2v_i.y-1, and whose B traces are v_i.x>=1. Suppose
all A traces are proper, all three ambient cap areas have one
common value Q, and a<b/32. Then

    Q>2(a+k+b)/9.                               (32)

In particular this applies if those three caps genuinely attain
the halfspace depth at (0,y); it does not infer their criticality
merely from their common mass.

*Proof.* Suppose Q<=2(a+k+b)/9. Each B trace has area zero
because B is contained in T; each A trace has nonnegative area,
so q_i<=Q. The middle caps cover the plane because sum_i v_i=0.
At least one therefore contains the centroid of K. Formula (30)
shows that every triangle cap containing its centroid has area
at least 4k/9. Hence

    4k/9<=Q<=2(a+k+b)/9,

and therefore k<=a+b. The true-facet erosion gives b<k, so
a/k<b/(32k)<1/32. It follows that

    q_i/k<=Q/k<=2(1+a/k+b/k)/9<65/144.

Theorem 6 supplies the contradiction, proving (32). QED.

This corollary treats all triangular K with the displayed matched
support values, including exact outer vertices. It neither claims
that an arbitrary middle body is triangular nor changes the actual
aligned support values by an unauthorized independent normalization.

## 9. Unequal support offsets with a bounded total

The individual matched support identities in Section 8 can be
replaced by an inequality on their sum. Let K be any triangle,
and define its actual aligned support offsets by

    t_i=h_K(-v_i), tau=t_1+t_2+t_3.

The t_i need not be equal or individually positive. The number
tau is positive because K is full-dimensional. Its aligned outer
triangle is {x:v_i.x>=-t_i for all i}; translating x and y shows
that this triangle has area tau^2/2. Its barycentric coordinates
are

    lambda_i(x)=(v_i.x+t_i)/tau,  sum_i lambda_i=1,
    min_K lambda_i=0.

**Theorem 8.** Replace the support hypothesis h_K(-v_i)=1 in
Theorem 6 by

    tau<=3.                                     (33)

Keep every other geometric and mass hypothesis, including the
original canonical B contained in T and the proper A cuts at
v_i.x=2v_i.y-1. Then the same conclusion holds: not all three
middle cap areas can be at most 65k/144.

Moreover, Corollary 7 holds with (33) in place of the individual
matched supports. In particular the conclusion applies whenever
the actual aligned outer support triangle of K has area at most
|T|=9/2, with its position and its unequal offsets fully retained.

*Proof.* The exact true-facet enclosure of a triangle gives

    A contained in p+(2-rho)K,
    B contained in -p+rho K,
    0<rho<2.

These formulas are in the original coordinates. For example,
they follow from the centered-facet construction in Section 5
by absorbing the centroid translation into p. Define

    c_i=[v_i.p+(rho-1)t_i]/tau,
    d_i=(1+t_i)/tau.

The outer-barycentric images of the two enclosures satisfy

    lambda_i(A) contained in c_i+(2-rho)lambda_i(K),
    lambda_i(B) contained in -c_i+rho lambda_i(K),
    sum_i c_i=rho-1.

Here the inclusion of coordinate-value sets is meant in the
ordinary scalar sense; it follows by applying the displayed
affine functional to the actual body containment. A proper A
cut provides a point with

    lambda_i(a)<2lambda_i(y)-d_i.

Since min_K lambda_i=0, its enclosure implies

    c_i<2lambda_i(y)-d_i.

Sum these strict inequalities and use
sum_i d_i=1+3/tau. This gives

    rho<2-3/tau<=1.                              (34)

In particular these hypotheses themselves force tau>3/2;
there is no unmentioned small-tau case admitting positive-volume
A,B. The strict rho<1 again implies b<k.

Let m_i=max_K lambda_i>0 and r_i=lambda_i(y)/m_i>0. The outer
homothet D=-p+rho K has lambda_i-maximum rho m_i-c_i and
lambda_i-width rho m_i. The restriction B contained in T becomes
lambda_i(B)<=d_i. Thus its support excess above this threshold is

    rho m_i-c_i-d_i>rho m_i-2lambda_i(y).

The identical contraction estimate gives

    b/k<=rho^2-(rho-2r_i)_+^2
          <1-(1-2r_i)_+^2.                       (35)

Using a<b/32 and k<=a+b now yields b/k>32/33 and hence
lambda_i(y)>(41/100)m_i, exactly as before. The three vertex
values of each lambda_i are again 0,u,v. The proof of Theorem 6
using the explicit centroid-tail formula (30) is unchanged.

For the common-cap corollary, the same three actual ambient
halfspaces have traces v_i.x>=2v_i.y-1 at A, v_i.x>=v_i.y
at K, and v_i.x>=1 at B. They cover the continuous middle
plane, irrespective of the support offsets. The identical
centroid argument gives k<=a+b under a hypothetical
Q<=2(a+k+b)/9. Equation (34) gives b<k, so the strengthened
q_i/k<65/144 follows and contradicts the first part. QED.

The case tau>3 is not included. In that case (34) only gives
rho<2-3/tau>1, so neither b<k nor the sharpened cap bound used
in Section 8 follows from this argument.
